title: Raptors' Barnes, Quickley, Murray-Boyles questionable vs. Grizzlies
text:
Raptors' Barnes, Quickley, Murray-Boyles questionable vs. Grizzlies - Sportsnet.ca 
 Loading... Raptors' Barnes, Quickley, Murray-Boyles questionable vs. Grizzlies
 Sportsnet Staff @Sportsnet November 09, 2026 - 4:34pm The Raptors Show's Blake Murphy and Matt Bonner discuss Scottie Barnes' performance in the Raptors' comeback vs. the Los Angeles Clippers, how he galvanized the group with his defence, and why his versatility is so important. 
 The status of three of the Toronto Raptors ' key players is in question on Monday.
 Scottie Barnes and Immanuel Quickley have both been listed as questionable for the Raptors' game against the Memphis Grizzlies. 
 Both players were limited participants in practice on Sunday, according to Sportsnet's Michael Grange. 
 Then, on Monday after the team's morning shootaround, it was announced that forward Collin Murray-Boyles had been downgraded to questionable with an illness.
 The Raptors also announced later that two-way players Malachi Smith and Kevin McCullar Jr. were available against the Grizzlies. It was the first time this season that Toronto made its two-way players available. 
 Barnes and Quickley each missed Friday's game against the Milwaukee Bucks with a left adductor/groin injury and right hamstring tightness, respectively. 
 An all-star last season, Barnes appeared to be labouring and favouring his hip during the third quarter in Wednesday's loss to the Denver Nuggets.
 Barnes, 25, has averaged 23.5 points, 7.6 rebounds, 5.1 assists and 2.3 steals in 33.3 minutes over eight games this season.
 It's unclear how or when Quickley suffered the injury, but he played 32 minutes in that same game. 
 The 27-year-old is averaging 17.4 points, 3.5 rebounds, 5.8 assists and 31.8 minutes in eight games.
 Meanwhile, Murray-Boyles is averaging 10.7 points, 5.8 rebounds and 1.3 assists in nine games this season. 
 The 21-year-old has started the Raptors' last three games as they continue to deal with injury concerns. He broke out for 19 points, seven rebounds, two assists, four steals and a block in Friday's 121-107 win over the Milwaukee Bucks.
 Star wing Kawhi Leonard also remains out while undergoing the return-to-play process after receiving treatment for left knee swelling. An update on Leonard's status is expected on Tuesday.
